traits.text: Always crits VS Grappled creatures.

tactics.harder: Focus 1 target, especially if they have disadvantage on rolls.

name: Griffon

actions.name: Fly & Drop
actions.text: (if Grappling) Fly upward 12 and release (6d6 fall damage, landing Prone).

flavor: Half-eagle, half-lion, and utterly majestic. Only reveals itself when finished with self-grooming.

tactics.easier: Stay low to the ground, and mostly use Talons.
tactics.harder: End turn in the air to avoid melee attacks. Use Fly & Drop as much as possible.

name: Bulette

traits.name: Burst Forth!
traits.text: Combat starts with the heaviest character making a DC 14 DEX save or they are Grappled and take 1d12+20 (half on save, escape DC 14).

actions.name: Drag Below
actions.text: (vs Grappled creature) 2d12 then drag below and burrow 6.

flavor: Stoneskinned ambush predators with shovel-shaped claws and a gaping maw. Their burrowing has been known to sink entire houses.

tactics.easier: Stay above ground, mostly using Leap & Bite.
tactics.harder: Drag Below as much as possible.

name: Troll

traits.name: Regenerate
traits.text: Does not die at 0 HP. Only fire, radiant, or a crit while at 0 HP can kill it.

tactics.easier: Switch between targets, mostly using Claws.
tactics.harder: Avoid heroes who can deal lethal damage (Mage, Oathbreaker, Cheat), and use Bite as much as possible.

tactics.easier: Attack with the Morningstar first, allowing heroes to avoid being hit while Prone.
tactics.harder: Attack with the Club first, increasing the chance of landing a crit with the Morningstar.

notes: Solo lvl 3 Ettin (header “Solo lvl 3, large bickering two-headed giant”); distinct from the lvl 9 Ettin. Last Stand is printed as “DYING.”; HP is flat 120. Group RP Note: If an Ettin hits on the first roll, “ThAt gOoD HiT, hAhaHa!” If it hits on the 2nd roll “SEE?!”

name: Hill Giant

traits.name: Clumsy
traits.text: Always attacks with disadvantage.

actions.name: Punt
actions.text: 1d12+10. On hit, Prone & Knockback Primary Die spaces.

flavor: The smallest of giantkin; foul-tempered, petty, and deeply insecure about appearing foolish. Found commonly roaming the countryside, devouring livestock, and acting as hired muscle for Goblins, Bandits, and especially Gnolls.

tactics.easier: Punt Ranged heroes away to safety. Play into their stupidity, attack suboptimal targets (whichever is making the most noise, whichever hurt him last).
tactics.harder: Use Punt to separate heroes and kick them toward allies.

traits.name: Bloodthirsty
traits.text: Advantage VS damaged creatures.

name: Gnoll Hunter

traits.name: Bloodthirsty
traits.text: Advantage VS damaged creatures.

flavor: A natural tracker that never loses a trail and never forgets a scent.

tactics.easier: Mostly use melee attacks, attack undamaged heroes.
tactics.harder: Use ranged attacks to damage multiple targets.

name: Gnoll Packleader

traits.name: Bloodthirsty
traits.text: Advantage VS damaged creatures.

flavor: The first to taste blood in any battle, the Packleader drives his allies to victory.

tactics.easier: Bark Orders to move Gnolls adjacent to heroes after the gnoll has already attacked.
tactics.harder: Bark Orders to move Gnolls to safety after they’ve acted, or to give them extra movement needed to chase down heroes hiding behind the frontliners.

name: Gnoll Frenzied One

traits.name: Bloodthirsty
traits.text: Advantage VS damaged creatures.

traits.name: Frenzy
traits.text: Advantage when damaged.

flavor: Flurry of chaos with no thought for self-preservation.

tactics.easier: Target well-armored or undamaged heroes. Have them ignore the Packleader's commands.
tactics.harder: Bloodthirsty and Frenzy can stack, giving Advantage 2.

notes: Tactics lines continue at the top of the next column.

name: Gnoll Battle Shaman

traits.name: Battle Rattle
traits.text: All gnolls gain +2 speed and advantage while damaged.

actions.name: Baleful Howl
actions.text: DC 14 WIL save or Frightened 1 round. THEN:

actions.name: Withering Dread
actions.text: (Reach 10) 6d6 necrotic damage, divide these dice up amongst targets within reach.

flavor: A beacon of fear with an aptitude for unstable magic.

tactics.easier: Focus the Dread dice on 1 well-armored target.
tactics.harder: Whichever dice roll low on Withering Dread, damage unharmed allies. Spread the remaining dice out to make defending unappealing.

notes: Bloodthirsty is not printed in this block.

name: Briarbane Seedling
flavor: A juvenile sprout, Seedlings throw rock-hard seeds from hiding spots to assist their fellow warriors.

tactics.easier: Attack while heroes are adjacent. Attack Acidpods when they'll damage other Briarbanes.
tactics.harder: Target Grappled heroes, or Acidpods that are in a good position to explode and hit multiple enemies.

notes: Armor printed as “H*”; the asterisk refers to the Peeling Bark group trait.

name: Briarbane Acidpod

traits.name: Caustic Eruption
traits.text: On death: 4d6 to ALL in Reach 1.

flavor: Acid-bloated viney tangles, Acidpods have no sense of individuality and will gladly sacrifice themselves for the safety of the forest. Their remains have proven to be effective fertilizer for other horrifying plant creatures.

tactics.easier: Grab isolated or well-armored or high DEX heroes.
tactics.harder: Grab heroes near their allies then shoot it with Seedlings for a big explosion! Combo with Tanglers to Pull heroes into a clump.

notes: Armor printed as “H*”; the asterisk refers to the Peeling Bark group trait.

name: Briarbane Tangler

traits.name: Remember!
traits.text: Tiny/Small creatures are affected twice as much by forced movement; Large, half as much.

actions.name: Tangle (2×)
actions.text: (Reach 6) 1d6+2, Grappled (escape DC 12, or any fire or slashing damage). OR:

flavor: A coiled mass of bark-armored roots capable of taking any shape, Tanglers are able to restrain many foes at once.

tactics.easier: Separate them from their allies. They're far less deadly without other creatures taking advantage of their Grapple.
tactics.harder: Act first amonsgt monsters to set up advantage on their attacks. Avoid heroes who deal fire or slashing damage.

notes: Armor printed as “H*”; the asterisk refers to the Peeling Bark group trait. “Remember!” is a boxed rules reminder inside the block.

name: Briarbane Rootbreaker
flavor: The frontline troops of the forest, these walking stumps strike with arms stronger than sledgehammers.

tactics.easier: Target Grappled heroes, likely breaking them free.
tactics.harder: Angle their attacks to push heroes into each other or toward Acidpods.

notes: Armor printed as “H*”; the asterisk refers to the Peeling Bark group trait.

name: Briarbane Treant

traits.name: Enrage
traits.text: Attack with advantage when unarmored.

flavor: An ancient tree brought to life, a single Treant stands guard at the center of each of the worlds greatest forests.

tactics.easier: Mostly use Slam, targeting well-armored heroes.
tactics.harder: Use Stomp as often as possible, including against heroes Grappled by allies.

notes: Armor printed as “H*”; the asterisk refers to the Peeling Bark group trait.

name: Duskprowler

traits.name: Illusory Aura
traits.text: Attacks against the Duskprowler have Disadvantage 2. Damage suppresses this effect until the end of the next hero’s turn.

flavor: Predatory cats capable of distorting perception, they blend into their environments to stalk their prey.

tactics.easier: Stay near heroes that use large damage dice to attack.
tactics.harder: Focus on attacking heroes with small damage dice (daggers, unarmed strikes, wind spells).

name: Owlbear

actions.name: Fearsome Hoot (1 use, Reach 12)
actions.text: Lower level enemies take 20 psychic damage – their WIL save. If they take 8 or more damage, they are Frightened as well (until the Owlbear is bloodied).

flavor: Aggressive and territorial, they are apex predators—stronger than bears and keener hunters than owls.

tactics.easier: Use Fearsome Hoot after you are bloodied.
tactics.harder: Use Fearsome Hoot early, so that Frightened lasts longer.

name: Wolf

traits.name: Pack Hunters
traits.text: Flee combat when outnumbered.

flavor: Pack hunters that surround and overwhelm prey much larger than themselves.

tactics.easier: Allow one wolf to take most of the damage at the beginning, so that Fearsome Howl goes away quickly. Have the Wolves flee early.
tactics.harder: Move in and out of melee range, so that it takes longer for any single wolf to die. Have the Pack Leader Interpose for wolves, to keep them from dying and fleeing.

groupTraits.name: Fearsome Howl
groupTraits.text: At the beginning of combat, heroes make a DC 13 WIL save or start Frightened. Ends when 1 wolf dies.

notes: Tactics are printed once for the Forest Wolves group.

name: Dire Wolf
flavor: A monstrous family of wolves with longer claws, sharper teeth, and piercing red eyes. Twice the size of a regular wolf.

tactics.easier: Allow one wolf to take most of the damage at the beginning, so that Fearsome Howl goes away quickly. Have the Wolves flee early.
tactics.harder: Move in and out of melee range, so that it takes longer for any single wolf to die. Have the Pack Leader Interpose for wolves, to keep them from dying and fleeing.

groupTraits.name: Fearsome Howl
groupTraits.text: At the beginning of combat, heroes make a DC 13 WIL save or start Frightened. Ends when 1 wolf dies.

notes: Tactics are printed once for the Forest Wolves group.

name: Dire Wolf Pack Leader

traits.name: Protector of the Pack
traits.text: (Reach 6) Can Interpose.

tactics.easier: Allow one wolf to take most of the damage at the beginning, so that Fearsome Howl goes away quickly. Have the Wolves flee early.
tactics.harder: Move in and out of melee range, so that it takes longer for any single wolf to die. Have the Pack Leader Interpose for wolves, to keep them from dying and fleeing.

groupTraits.name: Fearsome Howl
groupTraits.text: At the beginning of combat, heroes make a DC 13 WIL save or start Frightened. Ends when 1 wolf dies.

notes: Tactics are printed once for the Forest Wolves group. Its own flavour and tactics lines are draft placeholders (“XX”, “xx”) in the source.

name: Druid

actions.name: Beastshift
actions.text: +4 speed, gain Medium armor this round. 4d4+10. OR:

actions.name: Hurricane
actions.text: (Reach 3, AoE ) 4d4+10 to enemies. On damage: move targets anywhere within Reach.

flavor: Guardians of the wilds, they command the elements to strike back against the enemies of nature.

tactics.easier: Use Beastshift to charge into combat aggressively. Keep melee heroes nearby with Hurricane.
tactics.harder: Push heroes into obstacles or hazards with Hurricane. Use Beastshift to strike then escape melee.

name: Spring Golem

traits.name: Swiftspear
traits.text: (1/Round, Reach 2) Reaction: When an enemy escapes Entangle, strike them for 2d8.

actions.name: Verdant Growth (2x)
actions.text: (Reach 8) 2d8, Entangle: half speed (escape DC 12, or any slashing/fire damage). OR:

flavor: Embodiments of growth and rebirth, these are walking saplings into humanoid form, draped in flowers and vines.

tactics.easier: Stay away from Entangled foes, preventing you from using Swiftspear on them if they escape.
tactics.harder: Always move toward Entangled foes, so you can use Swiftspear. If you have at least 2 foes Entangled, use Crushing Vines.

name: Dryad

actions.name: Dryad Magic
actions.text: (Reach 6) 1d6+10. Gain an additional Dryad Magic effect based on the roll.

flavor: Beautiful, lithe beings who…

tactics.easier: Stay within your home tree, even after it is attacked.
tactics.harder: Immediately teleport to another tree within sight after your bonded tree is attacked. Distract them by attacking from a non-bonded tree.

groupTraits.name: Treebonded
groupTraits.text: Each Dryad is bonded to 1 specific tree, they only take damage when it does.

groupTraits.name: Treestep
groupTraits.text: Dryads inhabit trees and can teleport between any trees they can see.

groupTraits.name: Dryad Magic
groupTraits.text: Sum the attack dice, it gains the following effect: 2–3. Branch Sweep. Prone. 4–6. Rootlash. Restrained (Escape DC 10+dryad lvl, or any slashing damage). 7–8. Befuddled. Your next attack MUST be against an ally. 9-10. Thornburst. Teleport up to 6 away, then (Reach 2) 3d6 damage to allies. 11+. Glamorized. The next 2 actions you spend are controlled by the GM (you regain the spent actions afterward).

notes: Flavour line is unfinished in the draft. Dryad Tactics intro: “Assessing or RP comments from the Dryad should honestly reveal which tree is theirs! Perhaps they giggle when the wrong tree is attacked, or wince in pain when theirs is attacked. Let it be a puzzle to figure out which tree they are bonded to (but don’t make it too hard or you risk it turning into a frustrating slog!).” Dryad Magic is a shared results table, stored in groupTraits.

name: Snake Swarm

traits.name: Swarm
traits.text: Can enter the space of other creatures. When damaged, reduce HP by 1. AoE attacks reduce HP by 2.

actions.name: Venomous Bites
actions.text: (Reach 0, AoE) HPd4. On damage, Poisoned (healing ends)

tactics.easier: Overlap space with a small number of heroes. Clump together, making AOEs do more damage.
tactics.harder: Enter the spaces of as many heroes as possible. Spread out, to put pressure on the whole party and make AOEs less effective.

groupTraits.name: Swarms
groupTraits.text: If it makes sense, any creatures within a swarm when it is attacked may also take damage!

notes: Habitat assumed Forest (Swarms falls inside the Forest chapter). Section note: “If your party doesn’t like snakes or spiders, feel free to change them to rats, hornets, centipedes, beetles, bats or any other creature more appropriate for your table.” Tactics printed once for both swarms.
